methodology: Unchanged from AQ-01: pages classified as thin if the visible body (excluding nav, footer, JSON-LD, breadcrumb, and boilerplate disclaimer text) contains no original explanatory prose. Each finding below re-verified directly against live pages; status reflects what AQ-02A actually changed, not what it targeted.

findings.title: Food-ingredient leaf/entity pages contain zero original prose
findings.evidence: Every previously-cited page (foods/almonds, fruits/marionberry, sweet-flavors/ruby-cacao, vegetables/chayote, grains-starches/farro, legumes/fava-bean, herbs-spices/berbere, sauce-condiments/bearnaise, fungi/chanterelle) now opens with a genuine 'About This Entry' section rendering the entity's authored `summary` field, verified directly. AQ-02A's own QA pass reports 1,252/1,252 authored summaries rendered with zero empty-section violations; this rerun independently spot-checked 7+ pages and confirms it.

findings.title: Deprecated protein-food (foods/) leaf pages are equally thin duplicates of their canonical replacements, still live
findings.note: The thinness half of this finding is resolved — both foods/almonds/ and nut-seeds/almond/ now carry genuine narrative content. The duplication half is unchanged: 51 pages remain marked redirect_required with zero matching entries in _redirects, and both URLs are still live. This is arguably a subtler problem now than before: two equally polished, differently-framed pages describing the same entity under two different taxonomies, with no disclosure of the relationship on either page, verified by re-reading both foods/almonds/ and nut-seeds/almond/ directly.
findings.root_cause: Unchanged — incomplete migration, out of AQ-02A's publication-layer scope.

findings.title: Group and category hub pages have no narrative prose across any sampled domain
findings.evidence: groups/mushrooms/, groups/beef/, fruit-categories/fruit/ and other sampled hubs now render 'About This Group'/'About This Category' sections from the entity's `summary`/`introduction`-derived narrative. groups/beef/ additionally now renders a genuine, previously-invisible FAQ ('Why is beef the classic red wine pairing?' / 'Do all beef cuts pair with the same wine?') — this specific gap (group-tier FAQ rendering) was itself missing from AQ-02A's first pass and was caught and fixed during its own QA verification, confirmed here by re-reading the live page.

findings.title: Seasonal/occasion guides are short stub pages, not the long-form editorial content their nav placement implies
findings.evidence: christmas-wine-pairing-guide.html, thanksgiving-wine-guide.html, romantic-dinner-wine-guide.html, summer-bbq-wine-guide.html are untouched by AQ-02A (wine-education tier, not food-ontology). Word counts and structure unchanged from AQ-01.

findings.title: Region pages beyond the flagship /regions/usa/ are noticeably thinner and lack a beginner-explanation section present elsewhere in the same content family
findings.evidence: regions/ is entirely outside AQ-02A's scope (wine-education domain, not food-ontology). Unchanged.

findings.title: Serving pages lack the 'Beginner explanation' depth present in faults/ and techniques/
findings.evidence: serving/ is outside AQ-02A's scope. Unchanged.

findings.title: Generic templated meta descriptions on ingredient pages ignore a better-written field already available
findings.evidence: Re-checked fruits/marionberry/index.html: <meta name="description" content="Marionberry (Berries) — Fruits fruit"> — unchanged. AQ-02A rendered `summary` and `beginner_notes`/`faq` into the page body but did not wire the catalog's `seo_description` field into the page's <meta> description or <title>; the generic templated pattern from AQ-01 still ships in the <head> of every one of these now-content-rich pages.

findings.title: One authored catalog summary contains a grammar defect that would ship as-is if rendering were fixed naively
findings.evidence: legumes/fava-bean's summary ('...ingredient — beans use in global pulse cooking pairs with earthy reds...') is now live on the page, grammar defect and all, exactly as AQ-01 predicted would happen if rendering were fixed 'naively.' AQ-02A did not run a copy-edit pass on the ~950 summary fields before publishing them — this instance confirms the risk AQ-01 flagged was real, not hypothetical.
findings.root_cause: Content authoring defect in source data, now live. Scope beyond this instance unverified — recommend a copy-edit spot-check pass, see recommended-improvements.md.

findings.title: Group/category `introduction` field is extracted into the narrative pipeline but never rendered
findings.evidence: lib/food-publication/narrative.js's NARRATIVE_FIELDS registry includes `introduction` for both group and category tiers, and it is correctly extracted into every group/category projection's `narrative` object — but no renderer helper or call site ever reads `narrative.introduction`. Confirmed directly: fruit-categories/fruit/'s catalog `introduction` field ('The Fruit Ontology catalogs canonical culinary fruits...') does not appear anywhere in the rendered page, though its sibling `summary` field does. This is the one place AQ-02A's own Rule 2 ('no field without publication intent — render it or document the suppression') isn't fully satisfied: the field is captured but neither rendered nor documented as intentionally suppressed.
findings.root_cause: Renderer gap identified during this rerun's verification pass, not caught by AQ-02A's own QA (which checked summary/beginner_notes/faq rendering but not introduction).

summary_counts.pages_still_thin_or_undisclosed: 51 (TC-02 duplicate disclosure) + 4 (TC-04) + 47 (TC-05) + 40 (TC-06) + 73 (TC-09, minor) ≈ 215 pages with a residual finding, down from ~1,240 before AQ-02A
